name: Claudio Ranieri
scopeNote: Proposed by the researcher (user asked not to stop for confirmation): ONE counted spell, Leicester City 2015-17, because it is the signature era (2015/16 Premier League title) and the only one with dense tactical coverage found (Spielverlagerung, Sports Illustrated, Opta/Sky data). The 2015/16 title season is the core; the 2016/17 months are kept only as evidence of what happened after Kante left and Ranieri changed shape, not as the style. Style term used by sources: a compact 4-4-2 / 4-4-1-1 with zonal marking with man-orientations (Spielverlagerung) in a mid-low block, built on counter-attacks (Premier League: 'compact 4-4-2 system built to counter-attack'); 42.43% possession, lowest of any PL champion since 2003/04. Popular label 'catenaccio/Italian defensive' is rejected by SI (his approach is 'a bit more advanced than that', Sacchi-style zonal). Caveat for the low-block-counter-attack ideology: SI and Spielverlagerung describe a compact, fairly high-for-English-football line with 'high' pressure when the ball goes wide, so 'low block' is only partly supported: Spielverlagerung calls it a 'mid-low block'. Spells with titles at Valencia (Copa del Rey 1999) and earlier Chelsea/Monaco/Roma/Inter/Fulham/Nantes were not mined: no tactical evidence gathered in this run. Appointment 2015-07-13 (FourFourTwo); sacking 2017-02-23 (theScore, 'lost his job Thursday', dated 2017-02-23).
openQuestions: Block depth: Spielverlagerung says 'mid-low block' and that lack of speed prevents a higher line; SI says the back line is 'high enough to catch a forward offside' and describes Sacchi-like squeezing with Schmeichel kicking long so 'it can press high'. Sources disagree on how low the block was; the 'low-block' label is not clearly supported.
Should Valencia 1997-99 (Copa del Rey) or Chelsea 2000-04 be added as counted spells? No tactical sources mined for them; Sacchi influence is only claimed by SI for Leicester.
Corriere della Sera Italian original of the 'afraid of Italian tactics' interview not found; English translation via Telegraph/FourFourTwo only.
Set-pieces: only one in-period fact (Ranieri says Leicester were usually solid at corners/free-kicks, from 2016/17) and no data on routines; man vs zonal at set-pieces not found.
Zonal Marking (Michael Cox), Coaches' Voice and These Football Times returned no Ranieri pages in site: searches; Jonathan Wilson not found.

sources.title: PL30: How Ranieri masterminded Leicester's title victory
sources.evidence: The Italian made the switch to a compact 4-4-2 system built to counter-attack with devastating efficiency.

sources.title: PL30: How Ranieri masterminded Leicester's title victory
sources.evidence: Leicester, who had used 11 different formations the year before, stuck with this 4-4-2, which became a 4-4-1-1 out of possession, in 35 of their 38 matches.

sources.title: PL30: How Ranieri masterminded Leicester's title victory
sources.evidence: One of Ranieri's most decisive early calls was to move away from the back-three set-up that had worked so well during the closing stages of 2014/15.

sources.title: PL30: How Ranieri masterminded Leicester's title victory
sources.evidence: His plan was to operate with two disciplined banks of four, with an energetic deep-lying striker operating behind a speedy centre-forward, who could punish opponents on the break.

sources.title: PL30: How Ranieri masterminded Leicester's title victory
sources.evidence: Realising their goal threat was enhanced by game plans that revolved around transitions, Leicester are the only champions to have adopted a non-possession-based strategy.

sources.title: PL30: How Ranieri masterminded Leicester's title victory
sources.evidence: Their average possession figure (42.43 per cent) is by some distance the lowest on record for a Premier League winning team, since such data started being collected in 2003/04.

sources.title: PL30: How Ranieri masterminded Leicester's title victory
sources.evidence: The Foxes' resolute defensive shape proved hard to break down. And rival teams, perhaps showing a degree of complacency, continued to leave themselves open to counter-attacks.

sources.title: PL30: How Ranieri masterminded Leicester's title victory
sources.evidence: During an astonishing campaign in which they lost only three times, Ranieri made just 33 changes to his starting XI.

sources.title: PL30: How Ranieri masterminded Leicester's title victory
sources.evidence: The little-known French midfielder cost £5.6million from Caen and was a revelation in central midfield. His 175 tackles and 156 interceptions were the most in the division.

sources.title: Arsenal - Leicester City 2:1 (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Ranieri picked the same starting eleven for the sixth consecutive match as they featured in their usual 4-4-2 formation

sources.title: Arsenal - Leicester City 2:1 (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Ranieri’s side have been a welcome change in the Premier League as they employ a zonal marking system with man-orientations which sees them stay stable and compact in a 4-4-1-1 shape.

sources.title: Arsenal - Leicester City 2:1 (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Within such a defence, a team will organize themselves zonally where the primary reference point for the defenders is the opposition. When not tasked with covering a nearby attacker, the team will maintain their shape in their base positions and cover the space in a zonal structure.

sources.title: Arsenal - Leicester City 2:1 (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Leicester’s compactness must also be noted as it plays an important role in their organisation. Through the zonal scheme they maintain their shape and do so with strong distances both horizontally and vertically. There were some issues in the spatial compactness, with some open spaces between the midfield and defence but they generally restricted Arsenal’s access through good pressure.

sources.title: Arsenal - Leicester City 2:1 (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Arsenal’s dominance of possession against Leicester’s mid-low block suggests a control that they very rarely had, which was in many ways because of their sub-par spacing.

sources.title: Arsenal - Leicester City 2:1 (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Through their zonal defence, they maintained a clear shape and the wingers didn’t closely mark the Arsenal full-backs – a role which most wingers are accustomed to in the English leagues. Instead they would maintain good spacing between the full-back and the centre of the pitch, meaning that they could provide strong support to the midfield pairing.

sources.title: Arsenal - Leicester City 2:1 (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Leicester are one of the strategically strongest teams in England this year through their stable defending and great transition game

sources.title: Arsenal - Leicester City 2:1 (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Danny Simpson’s dismissal was a pivotal moment in the game as Leicester moved to a 4-4-1 with Gray and Wasilewski replacing Mahrez and Okazaki.

sources.title: Tactical breakdown: How Ranieri's Leicester City has overtaken the EPL (SI)
sources.evidence: The Foxes line up in a standard English 4-4-2, with Riyad Mahrez’s tendency to drift inside and next to the front two passing as their most complicated wrinkle.

sources.title: Tactical breakdown: How Ranieri's Leicester City has overtaken the EPL (SI)
sources.evidence: With how close Leicester’s players sit in their defensive starting positions, opponents have to break down three lines of pressure in quick succession to get behind without hitting a ball over the top. If they go long, the back line is usually high enough to catch a forward offside, or goalkeeper Kasper Schmeichel can easily deal with overhit passes.

sources.title: Tactical breakdown: How Ranieri's Leicester City has overtaken the EPL (SI)
sources.evidence: As the opposition builds out of the back, wingers Mahrez and Marc Albrighton pinch in toward the middle, enticing wide play. Once the ball moves left or right, the near-side forward and winger can close down and win the ball back or force a long ball that Leicester’s defenders can win.

sources.title: Tactical breakdown: How Ranieri's Leicester City has overtaken the EPL (SI)
sources.evidence: Once it wins the ball—Leicester has a league-high 357 interceptions, indicative of its pressing ability—the club tries to get forward as quickly as possible. That often includes going wide to Albrighton or an overlapping fullback, or looking for a diagonal ball over the top from central midfield to Mahrez as he cuts inside.

sources.title: Tactical breakdown: How Ranieri's Leicester City has overtaken the EPL (SI)
sources.evidence: Schmeichel almost always looks long out of the back. In the last three matches, only two of the passes he attempted weren’t long. His passing percentage is poor, but Leicester prefers having the ball far away from its goal so it can press high.

sources.title: Tactical breakdown: How Ranieri's Leicester City has overtaken the EPL (SI)
sources.evidence: The Foxes squeeze the available attacking space and tend to leave opponents frustrated, even when the numbers would suggest that they should be outnumbered in the middle.

sources.title: Tactical breakdown: How Ranieri's Leicester City has overtaken the EPL (SI)
sources.evidence: Even on the counterattack, Leicester rarely finds itself with a numerical advantage. Even numbers is about as good as it gets, but that hasn’t been necessary with Vardy’s execution.

sources.title: Tactical breakdown: How Ranieri's Leicester City has overtaken the EPL (SI)
sources.evidence: The ball rarely stays centrally for very long before whoever is on it looks for a diagonal penetrative ball or at least a wide option.

sources.title: Il ritorno alla normalità del Leicester (Il Post)
sources.evidence: Schierato in campo con un 4-4-2, il Leicester non teneva molto la palla ma occupava bene le posizioni in campo. Ranieri sfruttava l’elevata velocità della squadra, comune a quasi tutti i giocatori fra centrocampo e attacco, per impostare contropiedi rapidissimi che in pochi passaggi riuscivano a portare i giocatori fino all’area avversaria.

sources.title: Il ritorno alla normalità del Leicester (Il Post)
sources.evidence: Il reparto offensivo è l’unico che è stato veramente rinforzato. Non è stato ceduto nessun giocatore, è arrivato Bartosz Kapustka, giovane promettente ala polacca, la punta nigeriana Ahmed Musa

sources.title: Il ritorno alla normalità del Leicester (Il Post)
sources.evidence: Gli avversari hanno ormai imparato ad affrontare il Leicester e non si fanno più cogliere impreparati dal pressing e dai rapidi contropiedi.
